bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Tightens Midday Meal Checks After Food-Quality Complaints
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Tightens Midday Meal Checks After Food-Quality Complaints Breaking News Bihar Tightens Midday Meal Checks After Food-Quality Complaints By Maria Dsouza November 7, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar has ordered headmasters of government and government-aided schools to taste and certify midday meals before they are served to students, following complaints about poor food quality. The directive requires a daily record confirming that the meal was tasted, found satisfactory and considered fit for consumption. The order was communicated through an IPRD communique on Friday, which said the directorate of the Mid-Day Meal Scheme had instructed all district education officers to enforce the procedure in schools. The directive places responsibility for the immediate pre-serving check on the school’s headmaster, teacher-in-charge or principal teacher. Under the new procedure, the designated school official must taste the meal every day before it is distributed to students. The official must then certify that the food was tasted, was satisfactory and was fit for consumption. The requirement applies to schools covered by the state’s government and government-aided education system. If the headmaster, teacher-in-charge or principal teacher is absent, a nominated teacher must carry out the tasting and certification. This provision ensures that the daily check does not stop because the school’s senior officials are unavailable, according to the reported directive. The certificate must be signed by the headmaster or teacher-in-charge and retained in the school’s records. These records are intended to be available for official verification, creating a documentary trail for district education authorities to check whether the procedure has been followed. The directive comes after reports of poor-quality food in schools, making the school-level certification process the latest administrative response to concerns over the midday meal system. While the order assigns a clear responsibility to school officials, the report does not specify any new testing arrangement, inspection schedule, penalty for non-compliance or changes to the agencies supplying the meals. The role of district education officers will be to enforce the instruction across the state’s government and aided schools. For students, the immediate change is that a designated school representative must taste the meal before serving and maintain a signed certificate in the school records. Further implementation details will depend on how the education authorities verify these certificates and respond to any future complaints about meal quality. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Expands Solar Power Plan for Rural Water Towers - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Expands Solar Power Plan for Rural Water Towers Breaking News Bihar Expands Solar Power Plan for Rural Water Towers By Maria Dsouza November 7, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed officials to raise the proposed capacity of solar panels on rural water towers from 5 kilowatts to 20 kilowatts, linking the expansion to improved panchayat services, energy savings and more reliable basic infrastructure. Choudhary issued the instructions while chairing a review meeting of the panchayati raj department at the Sankalp auditorium in Lok Sevak Awas. He asked officials to install the higher-capacity panels in a way that allows panchayats to derive greater benefits from the solarisation of rural water infrastructure. The original proposal presented at the meeting involved installing 5-kilowatt off-grid solar panels on water towers under the Chief Minister Gramin Peyjal Nishchay Yojana. Panchayati raj department secretary Manoj Kumar briefed the chief minister on the proposed scheme, its implementation procedures, annual electricity expenditure and the department’s responsibilities. The revised 20-kilowatt capacity is intended to support basic facilities in panchayats while reducing energy consumption and expenditure. The meeting also discussed how savings generated through solarisation could be used, although the department’s presentation did not specify the amount of savings expected or the facilities that would receive the funds. Choudhary asked officials to make the solarisation of Panchayat Sarkar buildings an integral part of construction estimates. He also directed the department to link the work to funds from the 15th Finance Commission and the 7th State Finance Commission to ensure timely availability of funds and faster implementation. The plan will involve the Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency, or BREDA. The department said BREDA’s role would cover implementation, financial management, maintenance and monitoring of the solar panels. An implementation and coordination committee is also proposed to oversee the programme. The review meeting additionally focused on monitoring electricity supply in panchayats. Choudhary ordered officials to regularly share information on the number of hours of power supply received by each panchayat with public representatives. A dedicated team is to be set up to send daily updates to the designated mobile numbers of panchayat mukhiyas, MLAs and MPs. The electricity-monitoring mechanism would create a regular flow of information on local power availability, but the department’s presentation did not state when the updates would begin or identify the system that would be used to collect and verify the data. Choudhary also directed officials to accelerate construction of Panchayat Sarkar buildings and ensure their maintenance and regular upkeep. He said contractors responsible for constructing the buildings should also be held accountable for maintenance through a mechanism that clearly defines their responsibilities and liability. The next steps are the preparation of implementation arrangements for the higher-capacity solar panels, coordination with BREDA and the identification of financing through the two Finance Commission funds. Officials are also expected to establish the team responsible for daily electricity-supply updates and clarify maintenance responsibilities for Panchayat Sarkar buildings. Share Copy

On 3 November 2026, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced that Bihar has become the first state in India to introduce a comprehensive Silt Management Policy to address recurring floods and promote the scientific utilisation of river silt. Key Points Silt Management Policy: Bihar has introduced the Bihar Water Sources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026. It aims to restore rivers and water bodies through scientific desilting. It seeks to improve river water-carrying capacity and reduce flood risks. Nadi Sanjeevani Initiative: An MoU was signed between the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and the Government of Bihar on 3 November 2026. It aims to utilise excavated silt in National Highway construction projects. Utilisation of Silt: 243 lakh cubic metres of silt will be utilised in 16 ongoing National Highway projects. Another 835 lakh cubic metres is proposed for 27 future projects, subject to technical suitability. Implementation: The Bihar Road Construction Department (RCD) will act as the nodal department. A State-level Coordination Committee will oversee implementation. Benefits of the Policy: Reduction in flood risks through scientific desilting. Restoration of rivers and water bodies. Protection of agricultural land affected by sand and silt deposition. Sustainable utilisation of silt in infrastructure development. Assistance to Farmers: Financial assistance of ₹20,000 per two hectares is provided to affected farmers for excavating deposited sand. bihar_raw_news.title: NHAI to Use Bihar River Silt for Highway Construction - RAHSTA Expo
bihar_raw_news.content: NHAI to Use Bihar River Silt for Highway Construction Infrastructure Transport Nov 06 2026 The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and the Bihar government have signed a Memorandum of Understanding for scientifically desilting water bodies and using suitable excavated silt in national highway projects. The initiative, named Nadi Sanjivani, Nadi Punarjeevan, Sadak Navnirman, is intended to address silt accumulation, seasonal flooding and the shortage of construction materials in the state. Rivers including the Ganga, Kosi, Gandak, Falgu and Bagmati carry substantial silt through Bihar. The accumulation reduces their water-carrying capacity and complicates water management, while the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has faced delays and higher costs because soil and ballast often have to be transported from distant locations. Under the agreement, 39.3 mn cubic metres of silt will be made available at no cost for ongoing highway projects. A further 105 mn cubic metres is planned for future projects. The NHAI will lead dredging using scientific methods, with the material being used for earthwork, embankments and subgrade construction. The NHAI is executing 39 projects covering 1,561 km in Bihar, with an investment of Rs. 583.4 bn. It has also proposed 11 projects covering 1,982 km at an estimated cost of Rs. 1.85 tn. The programme will cover waterways linked to projects including Manikpur-Sahebganj, Munger-Mirzachauki, the Bhagalpur Bypass-Rasulpur route and the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata corridor. The plan draws on Maharashtra’s Buldhana Pattern, under which excavated soil was used in highway construction while ponds and water bodies were widened and deepened. That initiative used 22.5 mn cubic metres of soil and increased water storage capacity by 22.5 mn cubic metres without cost to the state government. Bihar has also planned 1,800 km of expressways under Vision 2047, and successful desilting could support their construction. Tags: NHAI Bihar river desilting

national_raw_news.title: President, Prime Minister extend greetings on auspicious occasion of Diwali
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has extended her greetings to the all Indians living in India and abroad on the eve of Diwali today. In a message, the President said that the festival of Diwali marks the victory of virtues over negative tendencies. She added that the festival also signifies the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. She said that on this occasion, people worship Lord Ganesh for auspicious beginnings and well-being, and Goddess Mahalakshmi for prosperity. President Murmu also wished for good health, happiness and prosperity of every citizen of the country. She also urged everyone preserves the environment, live with harmony. The President also appealed to the youth to contribute in building a Viksit Bharat. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended his greetings on the occassion of Diwali. Sharing a video message on social media, Mr Modi said that the festival of lights illuminates the entire country and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. He wished that the festival and the times ahead bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone. The Prime Minister further said he celebrates Diwali with great enthusiasm and that, as in previous years, he would continue the tradition of celebrating the festival with the brave soldiers of the country.

national_raw_news.title: Defence Minister meets IAF personnel at Bagdogra; lauds their vigilance and operational readiness
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has called upon Air Force personnel stationed at Bagdogra to maintain a high level of operational preparedness and vigilance, considering the region’s strategic importance in safeguarding the security of north-eastern India. Mr Singh was speaking to Air Force personnel at Bagdogra Airport in Siliguri, before proceeding to Sikkim. He said the nature of modern warfare was changing rapidly and was no longer confined to conventional battles along the borders. Cyberattacks, drone warfare, proxy wars and information warfare, including the spread of misinformation through social media, had emerged as major security challenges. The Defence Minister stressed that military personnel must remain technologically aware and well-equipped to deal with these emerging threats. He said advanced technology alone could not ensure victory without courage, discipline, high morale and a strong sense of responsibility. Mr Singh also emphasised the need to strengthen cordial relations between the armed forces and local communities, saying that public support was an important pillar of national security. Highlighting the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, he said Indian startups and industries were making significant contributions to the development of drones, anti-drone systems and other advanced defence equipment. The armed forces were also adopting indigenous technologies and modern training methods to prepare for future challenges. The Defence Minister said every successful military operation was the result of collective teamwork, dedication and professional commitment. He added that the entire nation stood firmly behind its armed forces.

national_raw_news.title: Petroleum Ministry rejects claims of excessive ethanol in petrol; says E20 meets BIS standards
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has rejected the claims of Karnataka Government that fuel sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains excessive ethanol. The Ministry clarified that E20 petrol supplied by public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to the prescribed quality standards. It noted that E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline. The Ministry also said that 893 samples collected across 27 States and Union Territories, including 56 from Karnataka, meet the prescribed specifications. The Ministry added that all 56 samples tested in Karnataka conform to IS 17021 specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19 to 20 per cent. Earlier, the three oil marketing companies, Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, had clarified that the claims, as reported, were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. In view of the concerns raised, the three OMCs have requested the Karnataka Government to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the test methodology adopted for the reported findings. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said that the OMCs maintain established quality assurance systems across their supply and distribution networks to ensure that blended fuel meets the applicable BIS specifications before reaching consumers.

national_raw_news.title: Govt building modern sports ecosystem through Khelo India and TOPS, says PM Modi 06 Nov 2026 | 8:00 AM 622
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the government is building a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots programmes, Khelo India Centres and Olympic-standard training under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). Felicitating India’s Asian Para Games 2026 contingent for its record haul of 114 medals, Prime Minister urged the athletes to build on their success as they prepare for the Los Angeles 2028 Games. Prime Minister also recalled his appeal from the Red Fort encouraging young people to participate in a nationwide talent hunt with the Olympics in focus. He said Para-sports also receive equal priority under these initiatives. Interacting with the contingent at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi, PM Modi said the performance reflected India’s emergence as a major global sporting power. He congratulated the athletes, their families, coaches and trainers, saying the players had won both medals and the hearts of millions. India secured 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, alongside five world records and nine Asian records. Comparing the achievement with the country’s tally of 14 medals, including one gold, in 2010, PM Modi credited the athletes’ perseverance and dedication. The Prime Minister noted that 34 of the contingent’s 56 female athletes won medals, while Indian competitors swept all three podium positions in four events. The team also won nine gold medals on the final day. Highlighting individual performances, PM Modi said Mona Agarwal set a world record in para shooting, while Haney improved his own world record. He also praised Himanshu, Ravi and Jehan for overcoming physical challenges through their performances. Recalling the sacrifices behind sporting success, PM Modi spoke about Rinku, who lost his mother two months before the Games and held up her photograph after winning gold. “That moment made all of us emotional,” he said. The Prime Minister also highlighted the achievements of younger athletes, noting that 36 of the 61 debutants won medals and Sandeep set a world record on his debut. Describing sports as a means of personality development and nation-building, PM Modi said it teaches discipline, teamwork and the ability to recover from setbacks. He added that the expansion of sports infrastructure, equipment manufacturing and broadcasting was creating employment opportunities beyond the playing field.

national_raw_news.title: Delhi Fire Services gear up ahead of Diwali to deal with any eventuality 3 hours ago 66
national_raw_news.content: The festival of lights, Diwali will be celebrated tomorrow. The festival marks the victory of good over evil. In view of the festival, several arrangements have been made in the National Capital to ensure a safe and secure festival for all residents. The Delhi Fire Services has drawn up an extensive emergency response plan to deal with fire incidents during the Diwali festival. Talking to Akashvani News, Chief Public Relations Officer at Delhi Fire Service Abhilash Kumar Malik said that as part of the preparations, 71 fire stations, 50 Quick Response Vehicles and 20 Motorcycle First Responder units will be deployed on Diwali to tackle fire related incidents. He said that the deployment is aimed at reducing response time, particularly in congested markets and narrow lanes where conventional fire engines may find it difficult to reach quickly. Mr Kumar also informed that 15 additional locations will have dedicated water tenders placed on standby to deal with fire incidents. Major hospitals in Delhi are fully prepared to deal with the cases of burn injuries during Diwali. The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, has made special arrangements to handle cases of burn injuries. Talking to Akashvani News, Head of the Department of Burns and Plastic Surgery at AIIMS, Dr Maneesh Singhal, said that an adequate number of ICU beds are available and the strength of doctors has been kept more than three to four times than usual times, to handle any emergency situations. Delhi Police has also put in place robust security arrangements across New Delhi in view of the festival. It has also appealed to the public to celebrate an eco-friendly Diwali, use only green crackers and burst them strictly during the permitted time slots of 6 am to 7 am and 8 pm to 10 pm. Tomorrow on the occasion of Diwali, Delhi Metro train services on the Pink Line, Magenta Line and Grey Line which normally commence at 7:00 AM on Sundays, will begin one hour earlier at 6:00 AM from terminal stations. In a social media post, DMRC said that during the evening, the last Metro train service will commence at 10 PM from terminal stations of all Metro Lines, including the Airport Express Line, instead of the usual last train departure timing of 11 PM.

national_raw_news.title: CBSE releases 2027 board exam date sheet; exams begin 16th February
national_raw_news.content: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has released the date sheet for the Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations 2027. The examinations for both classes will begin on 16th February next year, with papers commencing at 10:30 AM. According to the official timetable, the Class 10 examinations will conclude on 9th March, while the Class 12 examinations will continue until 9th April. As per the notification, Class 10 students will appear for examinations in 83 subjects, while Class 12 students will take examinations in 121 subjects. The Board said the date sheet had been prepared after carefully considering more than 40,000 subject combinations to ensure that students do not face any clashes between examinations in the subjects they have opted for. Earlier, the Board had also announced the schedule for practical examinations and internal assessments for the 2026-27 academic session. For schools across India and abroad, practical examinations and internal assessments for Classes 10 and 12 will be conducted from 1st January to 13th February next year. However, for winter-bound schools, practical examinations will be held earlier, from 9th November to 19th December this year. More than 26.5 lakh students are expected to appear for the Class 10 board examinations, while over 19.8 lakh students will take the Class 12 examinations. Notably, the CBSE has released the date sheet 101 days ahead of the commencement of the board examinations. Students can access the detailed timetable on the Board’s official website, cbse.gov.in.

national_raw_news.content: India and the European Union have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with Horizon Europe, the bloc’s 93.5-billion-euro flagship research and innovation funding programme. Under the arrangement, Indian researchers, businesses and research organisations will be eligible to receive direct funding from Horizon Europe and lead international collaborative research projects under its second pillar, which focuses on global challenges and European industrial competitiveness. Once signed and ratified by both sides, the agreement is expected to come into effect in January next year. The programme covers key areas such as healthcare, Artificial Intelligence, digital technology, space, climate, energy and industrial development. The European Commission said the agreement marks a significant milestone in India-EU relations and will strengthen scientific cooperation, create new research opportunities and deepen their strategic partnership. Welcoming the development, EU Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation Ekaterina Zaharieva said the agreement would open up new opportunities for businesses, researchers and innovators on both sides to work together in developing future technologies. Horizon Europe currently includes 23 associated non-EU countries, ranging from the United Kingdom, Canada and Japan to South Korea and Switzerland. The association will enable Indian institutions to receive grants directly from the European Commission and allow Indian scientists to lead and coordinate major international research projects in the covered areas, on terms similar to those available to organisations in EU member states. The agreement is expected to give fresh impetus to India-EU scientific and technological cooperation and strengthen collaboration in emerging technologies and innovation.

Access the E-Library Government launches API integration between Startup India and I-STEM portals November 07, 2026 | Saturday | News For strengthening access to national research infrastructure image credit- pib The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India has launched API integration between the 'Startup India' portal and the 'Indian Science, Technology and Engineering Facilities Map' (I-STEM) portal. This initiative was implemented in collaboration with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The initiative was led by Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA), Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood. It aims to strengthen the linkages between the startup ecosystem and the country's research infrastructure, enabling DPIIT-recognised startups to discover and access existing scientific and testing facilities. Prof. Sood explained that this integration is more than just a digital interface; it is an institutional synergy that connects the needs of startups with the scientific infrastructure and technological capabilities available across the country. He emphasised that this can reduce research and development (R&D) costs, avoid duplication of expensive facilities, and ensure better utilisation of publicly funded infrastructure. Automatic verification of DPIIT-accredited status and seamless connectivity will streamline the process for startups and simplify the search for scientific equipment and research facilities. While this integration simplifies the process of searching for and requesting access to infrastructure, each request will be evaluated and approved by the relevant institution. In the future, a Single Sign-On (SSO) feature will be added, allowing DPIIT-accredited startups to access and utilise I-STEM's scientific infrastructure and research facilities directly through the Startup India Portal. national_raw_news.title: Atmanirbhar Bharat: Indian Air Force Ties Up With IIT Madras To Develop Indigenous ...
national_raw_news.content: Atmanirbhar Bharat: Indian Air Force Ties Up With IIT Madras To Develop Indigenous Secure Communication System For Airborne Applications Defence Atmanirbhar Bharat: Indian Air Force Ties Up With IIT Madras To Develop Indigenous Secure Communication System For Airborne Applications Swarajya Staff Nov 07, 2026 | Updated 08:52 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The Indian Air Force's Software Development Institute has signed a Memorandum of Agreement with IIT Madras and IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation to jointly design and develop an indigenous digital communication system for airborne applications. The agreement was finalised yesterday (6 November), with Air Vice Marshal Sarabjit Singh, Commandant of the Software Development Institute, and Dr MJ Shankar Raman, CEO of IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation, signing the document in the presence of Professor V Kamakoti, Director of IIT Madras. Through this collaboration, the IAF intends to undertake joint development with IIT Madras and IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation on advanced algorithms for communication systems and networking. The partnership will focus on creating secure, reliable digital communication solutions tailored for the demanding operational environment of modern air operations, essential for networked warfare capabilities. The indigenous development aims to reduce reliance on imported systems and bolster the operational efficiency of the IAF, contributing to the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision of self-reliance in defence technology. Key focus areas include advanced encryption protocols, secure data transmission, resilience against threats, scalability for airborne networks, and integration with existing defence systems. This marks the second collaboration between the IAF and IIT Madras on secure communication technology, following a similar Memorandum of Understanding signed in December 2025. The partnership exemplifies the growing synergy between India's armed forces and premier academic institutions, with IIT Madras contributing its expertise in advanced communication technologies and cybersecurity to create robust, indigenous solutions for the nation's defence requirements.
